questions.stem: Explain what happens when a row in a referenced table is deleted, considering referential integrity constraints.
markingGuide: Referential integrity ensures that foreign keys point to valid rows.
Deleting a referenced row can violate referential integrity.
Database systems may restrict deletion or use cascading delete to maintain integrity.
questions.explanation: When a row that is referenced by a foreign key is deleted, it can lead to referential integrity violation. To prevent this, databases may restrict the deletion or use cascading delete to automatically delete dependent rows.
